question.explanation:
Let $u = 4-x.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= -1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = -\textrm{d}u. \]

We also note that $ x = 4-u. $

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \int (2x+1)\sqrt{4-x} \, \textrm{d}x & = \int \Big(2(4-u)+1\Big)\sqrt{u} (-\textrm{d}u) \\[5pt] & = -\int (9-2u)\sqrt u \, \textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & = -\int \left(9u^{1/ 2} - 2u^{3/ 2}\right) \textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & =- \left(6 u^{3/ 2} - \dfrac 4 5 u^{5/ 2} \right) + C \\[5pt] & =-6 \sqrt{(4-x)^3} + \dfrac 4 5 \sqrt{(4-x)^5} + C \end{align*}

question.text: Given that $u = 1+x^2$, which integral is equivalent to $\displaystyle \int x^5\sqrt {1+x^2} \, \textrm{d}x?$
question.explanation:
Since $u = 1+x^2$, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 2x \quad\Longrightarrow\quad {x\textrm{d}x}=\dfrac{1}{2}\textrm{d}u. \]

We also note that $x^2 = u-1.$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \int x^5\sqrt {1+x^2} \, \textrm{d}x &= \int x^4\cdot\sqrt {1+x^2} \cdot x\textrm{d}x \\[5pt] &=\int (u-1)^2 \cdot \sqrt u \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & =\dfrac{1}{2} \int (u-1)^2 \sqrt u \,\textrm{d}u \end{align*}

question.explanation:
Let $u = 2x - 1 .$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x =\dfrac12 \textrm{d}u. \] We also note that $x = \dfrac{u+1}{2}.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \int x\sqrt {2x - 1}\, \textrm{d}x & = \int \dfrac{u+1}{2}\cdot \sqrt {u} \cdot\left(\dfrac 12\right) \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] & = \int \dfrac{u\sqrt u + \sqrt u}{4}\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & = \dfrac14\int (u^{3/2} + u^{1/2})\,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] & = \dfrac14\cdot\left( \dfrac25 u^{5/2} + \dfrac 23 u^{3/2}\right) +C \\[5pt] & =\dfrac{1}{10} (2x-1)^{5/2} + \dfrac 16 (2x-1)^{3/2}+ C\\[5pt] & =\dfrac{1}{10} \sqrt{(2x-1)^5} + \dfrac 16 \sqrt{(2x-1)^3}+ C \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating Indefinite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
Let $u = 2x+1.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = \dfrac{1}{2}\textrm{d}u. \]

We also note that $x = \dfrac{1}{2} (u-1).$

Computing our limits of integration, we get

$x$ $-1/2$ $3/2$
$u$ $0$ $4$

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

\begin{align*} \int_{-1/2}^{3/2} 4x\sqrt{2x+1}\, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{0}^{4} 4 \cdot \dfrac{1}{2} (u-1) \cdot \sqrt u\cdot \dfrac{1}{2}\textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{4} \left(u^{3/2}-u^{1/2}\right)\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &= \left.\left(\dfrac{1}{({5}/{2})}u^{5/2}-\dfrac{1}{({3}/{2})}u^{3/2} \right)\right |_{0}^{4}\\[5pt] &= \left.\left(\dfrac{2}{5}u^{5/2}-\dfrac{2}{3}u^{3/2} \right)\right |_{0}^{4}\\[5pt] &= \left(\dfrac{2}{5}\cdot4^{5/2}-\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot4^{3/2}\right)-\left(\dfrac{2}{5}\cdot0^{5/2}-\dfrac{2}{3}\cdot0^{3/2}\right)\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{64}{5}-\dfrac{16}{3}\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{112}{15}} \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating Definite Integrals of Algebraic Functions Using Substitution

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
Let $u = x+3.$ Then, we have \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}x = \textrm{d}u. \]

We also note that $x = u-3.$

Computing our limits of integration, we get

$x$ $1$ $6$
$u$ $4$ $9$

We can now solve the integral using our new variable $u,$ remembering to use the new limits of integration:

\begin{align*} \int_{1}^{6} \dfrac{3x+1}{\sqrt{x+3}}\, \textrm{d}x &= \int_{4}^{9} \dfrac{3(u-3)+1}{\sqrt u}\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &= \int_{4}^{9} \dfrac{3u-8}{\sqrt u}\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &= \int_{4}^{9} \left(3u^{1/2}-8u^{-1/2}\right)\, \textrm{d}u\\[5pt] &= \left.\left(\dfrac{3}{(3/2)}u^{3/2}-\dfrac{8}{(1/2)}u^{1/2}\right)\right |_{4}^{9}\\[5pt] &= \left.\left(2u^{3/2}-16u^{1/2}\right)\right |_{4}^{9}\\[5pt] &= \left(2\cdot9^{3/2}-16\cdot9^{1/2}\right)-\left(2\cdot4^{3/2}-16\cdot4^{1/2}\right)\\[5pt] &= \left(2\cdot27-16\cdot3\right)-\left(2\cdot8-16\cdot2\right)\\[5pt] &= \left(54-48\right)-\left(16-32\right)\\[5pt] &= 6-(-16)\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{22} \end{align*}
